L-series giver endings in the Preterit must be distinguished from additional l-recipient suffixes; both gift and recipient can be resumed by clitics. Contractions include liwole, gbènaxyo, gbàtliyo and lə+gbìnanxu, without establishing a different stem.
hule ḥaye with an addressee or the people present is a death euphemism; Aloho hule ʕumro with God as giver can instead bless or grant life. Do not collapse the opposite event readings.

The teaching dars, reporting takmil, statement ifada, support dastak, morale moral and merit puwane constructions show contact vocabulary in light-verb frames. Borrowing routes are hypotheses, not established from these verses.

Negative lawleliyo is filed as Preterit consistently with its affirmative huleliyo counterpart (PrS 15/62); lawwile is treated likewise at PrS 18/2 and 38/83. Past, habitual or conditional translation alone does not choose a form box.
I.5 is widened semantically to binding undertakings, preserving its number and noun government. qawl, soz and qrar overlap in promising, but their headwords and attested prepositions remain distinct.

Proposed ṭaʕne burden is checked against the duel and wife’s provocation contexts: Anstoß/taunt fits the events better than a literal burden. The ṭ/t lexical identity is still an editorial question.

lebo with give qebəl and an activity clause is a repeated ability/acceptance construction; there is no evidence here for treating the experiencer as an l-coded recipient. Reflexive courage and endurance instead overtly use l-ruḥ-.

Routine counts remain aggregate background only. Existing abundant give cells are not enlarged simply because every reader requested a better context; quotations prioritize new collocation heads and genuinely thin cells.

Batch 4 retains senses 7–10 and adds literal orientation 2b, qm-placement 11 and technical game-tagging 12. The latter is supported by explicit hand-contact and catch paraphrases in multiple game descriptions.
Abundant transfer and command/notification/promise cells are not enlarged. New quotations prioritize newly indexed nouns, the new constructions and remaining sparse sense/form cells.

Pledge partners recur with ʕam, qum, šan and before God; these vary argument or witness expression while the existing promise meaning remains. Give hand ratification is repeatedly linked to a subsequent promise.
Copied Cyrillic ә, diacritics, equals signs and edition typos remain source-faithful. Alignment conflicts or omitted target clauses block additions at 81/56 and 94/109.

Batch 5 retains all inherited sense numbers and all earlier numbered proposals. No further numbered sense is needed: new noun collocations enter Idiomatic phrases, while face orientation repeats 2b and stock tagging repeats 12.
